data.description:
## What
Write tests that validate recall and precision metric computation for the replay harness:
- recall_all: fraction of all incidents that would be challenged (>= 0.50 threshold)
- recall_holdout: fraction of held-out incidents (listed in holdout.txt) that would be challenged (>= 0.70 threshold)
- precision: fraction of fired challenges that correspond to a real incident (>= 0.50 threshold)

## Why
Core metric correctness must be verified before implementation. These tests are the definitive specification of metric semantics.

## Test file
tests/test-inference-recall-replay.sh (same file as T1)

## Test cases
- 10 incidents all challenged → recall_all=1.0, precision=1.0: PASS
- 10 incidents, 5 challenged → recall_all=0.5: PASS (at threshold); recall_all=0.4: FAIL
- Held-out split: holdout.txt contains incident_ids hashed via (hash(ticket_id) mod 3 == 0); verify recall_holdout computed only over that subset
- Precision: 8 challenges fired, 5 map to real incidents → precision=0.625 (>=0.5): PASS
- Precision: 10 challenges, 4 real incidents → precision=0.4 (<0.5): FAIL
- RECALL_RESULT signal present in stdout on success with fields: signal, recall_all, recall_holdout, precision, all_passed (bool)

## Fixture approach
- Create synthetic incidents.jsonl with known challenge-firing behavior
- Stub the affects_fields classifier invocation via a wrapper script (temp dir) that returns predictable results
- holdout.txt lists incident_ids with pre-computed hash membership

## Acceptance criteria
- Tests fail (RED) before implementation exists
- No implementation coupling — tests only check signal output and exit codes
data.title: RED: test inference-recall replay recall and precision metric computation
